title: Thomson Reuters Hit With Antitrust Case Over 'Killer' AI Deal
key_facts: On 1 Oct 2026 the Rubin Law Office (Carlsbad, California) filed a purported antitrust class action against Thomson Reuters in the US District Court for the Northern District of California.
It alleges that Thomson Reuters' $650 million purchase of Casetext, and folding it into Westlaw, was a 'killer acquisition' meant to remove a cheaper rival.
The firm says it went from paying $32.50 a month for Casetext to $111.48 a month for Westlaw Classic, with a three-year mandatory term and 4% annual increases.
It asks the court to certify a nationwide class and a California subclass, to award treble damages, and to order Thomson Reuters to divest, spin off or re-create Casetext as an independent company.
The complaint says Westlaw had no generative AI tools of its own before it bought Casetext, whose CoCounsel tool launched in March 2023.
Thomson Reuters did not answer the ABA Journal; a spokesperson told Bloomberg Law it 'has not been served with any complaint'.
quote_evidence: Thomson Reuters is facing a purported antitrust class action lawsuit over its massive $650 million acquisition and integration of Casetext into its Westlaw system.
A spokesperson told Bloomberg Law that "Thomson Reuters has not been served with any complaint related to this matter."
why_it_matters_hint: It tests whether buying an AI start-up and absorbing it can be attacked as an illegal 'killer acquisition'.
notes: Law360 original is paywalled (only subscription boilerplate); wrote from the ABA Journal report of the same complaint (also covered by Daily Journal and Bloomberg Law per RSS). Allegations only; no court ruling. Thomson Reuters is the parent company of the Reuters news agency, whose stories appear elsewhere in this report.
